page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-112 is a high-memory compute instance designed for intensive parallel processing tasks that require substantial physical memory. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 56 physical cores and 112 virtual CPUs with multithreading enabled. It integrates 896 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supported by core instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2. The server provision contains no integrated local storage and no bundled GPUs, necessitating external networked block storage for persistent data requirements.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, registering a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 164204.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 94622.94, both landing in the top 10% of evaluated systems. Cached memory throughput reaches 7672.69 GB/sec in 16 KB read tests, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidth achieve 274.66 GB/sec and 136.46 GB/sec respectively. PassMark memory testing scored 3158.12, reflecting strong data transfer rates under concurrent access. Single-threaded metrics are moderately strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1648.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2886.28.

The dense allocation of 112 dedicated vCPUs and 896 GB of memory provides high operational density for enterprise-scale workloads. Because the hardware relies purely on CPU compute and network storage, it delivers cost-efficient throughput for tasks that scale linearly across cores and require memory residency, avoiding the operational expense of GPU-accelerated or dedicated NVMe hardware. However, lack of local disk storage means disk-bound throughput is tied to network storage limits, and large-model LLM generation exhibits lower efficiency, as shown by 2.75 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

This instance configuration is suited for massive in-memory databases such as Redis, large-scale software compilation, batch ETL pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency scientific simulation or ray tracing workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-112 is a compute-focused instance tailored for memory-intensive, highly parallel workloads. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 architecture, it provides 56 physical cores and 112 dedicated vCPUs with 896 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-core computing and memory performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 94622.94 and cached memory bandwidth of 7672.69 GB/sec. Single-threaded execution remains average to strong, while multi-threaded tasks like software compilation and Redis operations achieve high throughput. The platform provides strong resource density and efficiency for CPU-bound applications that demand large working sets, making it well fitted for in-memory databases, batch data pipelines, enterprise backend services, and distributed compute workloads.
